points.quote: They sit next to the source in `src/vs/**/test/` folders (`common`, `browser`, `node` and `electron-*` variants).
Use `scripts/test.sh` or `scripts\test.bat`, which run in Electron. Add `--grep` or `--run <file>` to target specific tests.
`npm run test-browser` runs the browser-targeted tests with Playwright. `npm run test-node` runs the Node tests with mocha.

Many extensions also have integration suites. These include `extensions/vscode-api-tests`, which exercises the extension API. **How to run:** Use `scripts/test-integration.sh` or `scripts\test-integration.bat`.
`test/smoke/`. They drive a real VS Code UI. **How to run:** `npm run smoketest`, which compiles and then runs.

The runner infrastructure is in `test/unit/` ... `test/integration/` has `electron`, `browser` and `agentHost` subfolders. ... `test/smoke/`. ... `test/sanity/`, with a `containers` folder. These look like release and install checks of built products.
Compile or transpile first (for example `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`) when the tests need fresh output.
